claims.text: A page exists in the Pulumi docs at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ (the link target of the 'Provider support policy' card on the support index page).
The Pulumi provider support policy page describes how long Pulumi maintains each provider major version.
Pulumi provides long-term security updates for some providers (the provider support policy page identifies which providers get long-term security updates).
Pulumi does not automatically roll back changes made during an update if an error or failure occurs; it completes pending in-progress operations, then exits and reports the error.
Pulumi does not automatically query the cloud provider's live state before running `pulumi up` or `pulumi preview`; it compares the desired state in the program against the last recorded state.
`pulumi up --refresh` refreshes state and applies the desired state in a single step.
Pulumi Cloud provides built-in drift detection for automated drift detection and remediation on a schedule.
The page /docs/iac/concepts/state-and-backends/ has a section on 'Refreshing state'.
Pulumi auto-naming appends a random suffix to the logical name, letting Pulumi replace resources with less downtime by creating the replacement before deleting the old resource.
Auto-naming can be disabled on a per-resource basis.
Project or stack configuration can customize or disable auto-naming globally, per provider, or per resource type.

Pulumi Cloud manages a unique encryption key for every stack to encrypt that stack's secrets, configurable to use a custom secrets provider; encrypting the same value across two stacks yields different encrypted strings.
Passing `--secret` to `pulumi config set` encrypts the value so it can be persisted in `Pulumi.<stack-name>.yaml`.
During preview, update or destroy, Pulumi decrypts secrets, which are plain text during deployment execution and accessible via the Pulumi config object.
Pulumi does not use the Terraform engine in any way, though some Pulumi providers use open-source Terraform schemas to determine available resources, parameters and attributes.
Pulumi native providers are mapped directly to cloud provider APIs and do not use Terraform schemas.
Pulumi is a declarative tool that uses imperative languages to define end state; the language is not used for talking to the cloud provider API.
Pulumi uses strongly typed languages that support IntelliSense and the Language Server Protocol, so users rarely need to leave their IDE.
Pulumi experimental features are always opt-in, enabled with a flag, command, or environment variable such as `PULUMI_EXPERIMENTAL=true`.
Experimental Pulumi features may change or be removed at any time without a deprecation cycle and are not necessarily supported.
Pulumi focuses on actively supporting the latest released major version of the providers it maintains.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version for up to a year, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The provider support policy page at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ lists the covered providers and what a long-term support release contains.
Older provider major versions (beyond the previous major covered by security updates) receive no patches at all from Pulumi.
The Pulumi Registry shows the current version for all providers maintained by Pulumi.
Major provider versions typically include significant changes such as deprecations, new resources and new functionality that may require migration steps.
Minor provider versions typically include new resources, features, performance improvements and bug fixes without breaking changes.
In npm, the tilde operator (~1.2.3) allows patch updates on the current minor version.
Provider patch versions are primarily for bug fixes and security updates and are designed to be fully backward compatible.

Each major version of a Pulumi provider includes migration logic to smooth the upgrade from the immediately previous major version, but these migrations do not always work across multiple major versions.
Link targets exist: /docs/support/provider-support-policy/, /docs/support/faq/secrets-config/, /docs/support/faq/pulumi-cloud/, /docs/support/faq/policies/.
Pulumi actively maintains the latest released major version of every provider it publishes.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version for up to 12 months, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The providers receiving long-term support updates on eligible older versions are AWS, Azure Classic, Azure Native, Azure AD, Command, Docker Build, GCP, Kubernetes, TLS, and Vault.
Registry package pages exist at /registry/packages/aws/, azure/, azure-native/, azuread/, command/, docker-build/, gcp/, kubernetes/, tls/, and vault/.

The Pulumi provider LTS branch ships High/Critical CVE security patches: fixes for CVEs affecting the provider's code or its direct dependencies, and fixes for broken internal infrastructure on the LTS branch needed to ship them.

A Pulumi provider LTS release does not contain new upstream API versions, new resources or properties, performance improvements, non-security bug fixes, or compatibility with newer language runtime versions.
Pulumi LTS providers remain compatible with the version of the Pulumi engine they were frozen at, unless security fixes prompt otherwise.
Exactly one long-term support major version exists per covered provider at any time.

When major N+1 of a covered provider ships, it becomes the new N, the old N becomes the new LTS major, and the previous LTS major reaches end of life on the same day regardless of how much of its 12-month window remained.
Within the LTS major of a covered provider, only the latest minor version receives patches; earlier minors are frozen.
Pulumi provider LTS releases are available through the same standard package registries as current-major releases but are tagged differently.
Customers pinning to a specific major version of a Pulumi provider (recommended) automatically receive patch releases as they ship.
Pinning to a specific major version is the recommended way to consume Pulumi provider LTS releases.

At any time, exactly one major version of a covered provider is the LTS version, and older majors receive no patches; N is the latest released major, so if v3 is newest, v2 is N−1 and v1 and earlier are end of life.
The current major (N) of a provider is supported until N+1 ships and receives new features, new resources, bug fixes, security patches, dependency upgrades, and new upstream API versions.
The LTS version (N−1) is supported up to 12 months from N's release or until N+1 ships, and receives security updates in the provider's code or its direct dependencies.
Provider versions N−2 and older are end of life, not supported, and receive no updates.
The FAQ page /docs/support/faq/infrastructure/ contains a section 'What are the best practices for maintaining provider versions'.
Pages exist at /registry/ and /docs/support/getting-support/.
